strengths.detail: The organization directed <cite id="11">80.3% of its total expenses</cite> toward program services in FY2023, exceeding the <cite id="12">75% industry standard</cite>.
IRUSA holds a <cite id="13">perfect 97/100 score for Accountability & Finance</cite> from Charity Navigator and a <cite id="14">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>.
The charity maintains <cite id="15">18.0 months of working capital</cite>, providing a significant buffer for long-term operational stability.

strengths_deep_dive: Islamic Relief USA demonstrates positive financial health through its <cite id="16">fundraising efficiency of $0.19 per $1 raised</cite>, which is well within the range of high-performing nonprofits. This efficiency is paired with a <cite id="17">strong theory of change</cite> and a documented track record of <cite id="18">32 years in operation</cite>. Their ability to manage <cite id="19">$228,581,851 in total assets</cite> while maintaining low liabilities of $5,280,117 indicates a sophisticated financial infrastructure capable of sustaining large-scale humanitarian interventions.
rich_narrative.summary: Islamic Relief USA (IRUSA) operates as a major humanitarian institution, managing <cite id="1">$165,235,589 in total revenue in FY2023</cite>. Founded in <cite id="2">1994</cite>, the organization provides a wide range of services including <cite id="3">water programs, orphan sponsorship, and disaster management</cite> across more than 40 countries. IRUSA is a primary destination for faith-based giving, maintaining a <cite id="4">verified Zakat-eligible status</cite> that aligns with traditional categories of need. While the organization has historically shown strong growth, it faced a recent <cite id="5">11% revenue decline in FY2024</cite>, bringing total revenue to $147,232,658. Despite this fluctuation, the charity maintains <cite id="6">a 97/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting high standards of accountability. The organization’s scale allows it to deliver massive relief, such as providing <cite id="7">187,563 food parcels and hot meals</cite> and <cite id="8">restoring critical health services for 1.5 million people</cite>. IRUSA serves as a significant grantmaker, distributing <cite id="9">$162,398,577 in foreign grants</cite> to support international implementing partners. This large-scale model ensures that donor funds reach high-urgency zones like <cite id="10">Gaza, Yemen, and Sudan</cite>.
